Title: Maturation of medial efferent system function in humans.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: human adults, term and premature neonates
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE primary tones with contralateral broadband noise
Outcome: contralateral suppression present at 1500 and 3000 Hz, absent at 6000 Hz; premature neonates showed suppression or enhancement
Evidence_Quote: at three f2 frequencies: 1500, 3000, and 6000 Hz

Title: Modeling otoacoustic emissions by active nonlinear oscillators.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: no subjects (theoretical model; neonatal OAE data used for comparison)
Stimulus_Type: theoretical oscillator models of spontaneous and evoked otoacoustic emissions
Outcome: data incompatible with Van der Pol oscillator; proposed oscillator better reproduces OAE phenomenology
Evidence_Quote: with characteristic damping coefficients in the 20-200 Hz range

Title: Maturation of human fetal responses to airborne sound in low- and high-risk fetuses.
Journal: Early human development
Target_Age: low- and high-risk preterm fetuses at 27, 30, 33, and 36 weeks GA
Stimulus_Type: airborne sound trials
Outcome: cardiac acceleration and body movement responses began at 30 weeks GA; cardiac threshold decreased with maturation
Evidence_Quote: received three sound trials at 90, 100, 105 and 110 dB

Title: Chronic placental insufficiency has long-term effects on auditory function in the guinea pig.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: guinea pigs (prenatally compromised and controls), tested at 8 weeks of age
Stimulus_Type: clicks and tone pips (auditory brainstem responses)
Outcome: no ABR threshold differences; increased wave III latency and I-III interval at high click rates in compromised animals
Evidence_Quote: tone pip stimuli at frequencies of 2, 4, 8, 16 and 32 kHz

Title: Chronic intracochlear electrical stimulation in neonatally deafened cats: effects of intensity and stimulating electrode location.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: chronic intracochlear electrical stimulation
Outcome: stimulation at 2 dB above EABR threshold partially prevented spiral ganglion neuron degeneration; effect depended on electrode position
Evidence_Quote: at an extremely low intensity (2 dB above electrically evoked auditory brainstem response threshold)

Title: Cochlear maturation and otoacoustic emissions in preterm infants: a time-frequency approach.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: click-evoked otoacoustic emissions (wavelet time-frequency analysis)
Outcome: CEOAE levels increased and latency decreased with postconceptional age until about 38 weeks, then term-like
Evidence_Quote: decomposed into 12 frequency bands, spanning the 0.25-6.25 kHz range

Title: Characteristics of the audio sound generated by ultrasound imaging systems.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: no subjects (theory and water-tank experiments; fetal exposure discussed)
Stimulus_Type: ultrasound imaging pulses (radiation-force generated audio sound)
Outcome: scanner-generated audio sound may reach close to 100 dB in the audible range, suggesting fetal exposure during ultrasound examinations
Evidence_Quote: with a typical spatial-peak pulse-average intensity value at 2 MHz may generate a localized sound-pressure level close to 100 dB

Title: Effects of aspirin on distortion product otoacoustic emission suppression in human adults: a comparison with neonatal data.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: human adults (aspirin-induced OHC dysfunction; sensorineural hearing loss) and term newborns
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE (2f1-f2) ipsilateral suppression
Outcome: aspirin altered suppression at 6000 Hz only; neither aspirin nor SNHL produced neonatal-like suppression
Evidence_Quote: DPOAE suppression was measured at f2 = 1500 and 6000 Hz

Title: Effects of middle-ear immaturity on distortion product otoacoustic emission suppression tuning in infant ears.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: human infants (birth to 6 months) and adults
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE input/output functions and suppression tuning (middle-ear/cochlear model)
Outcome: middle-ear immaturity explained infant-adult DPOAE differences; cochlear mechanics mature at birth
Evidence_Quote: DPOAE suppression tuning at f2= 6000 Hz was similar

Title: Ear asymmetries in middle-ear, cochlear, and brainstem responses in human infants.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: otoacoustic emissions (DPOAE/TEOAE) and auditory brainstem responses
Outcome: right-ear dominance for TEOAE and ABR; no left-ear dominance for DPOAE signal; middle-ear asymmetries did not explain the effects
Evidence_Quote: evaluated separately and across frequencies (1.5, 2, 3, and 4 kHz)

Title: Transient evoked otoacoustic emission latency and estimates of cochlear tuning in preterm neonates.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: transient evoked otoacoustic emissions (latency analysis)
Outcome: latency decreased with postconceptional age only in right ears within the 1.5-2.5 kHz range; tuning estimates decreased
Evidence_Quote: in the 1.5-2.5 kHz frequency range only

Title: Effects of neonatal deafening and chronic intracochlear electrical stimulation on the cochlear nucleus in cats.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: newborn kittens, neonatally deafened, implanted at 10-16 weeks of age
Stimulus_Type: chronic intracochlear electrical stimulation
Outcome: deafening reduced cochlear nucleus spherical cell density, area and volume; chronic stimulation did not reverse these changes
Evidence_Quote: at 6 dB above

Title: Rapid development of a sensory attribute in young chickens.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: background tone frequency changes (habituation, peeping delay)
Outcome: consistent ranking of the frequencies emerged within the first postnatal day
Evidence_Quote: five frequencies between 500 and 608 Hz

Title: Distortion-product otoacoustic-emission suppression tuning in human infants and adults using absorbed sound power.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE suppression tuning curves (absorbed sound power)
Outcome: infant and adult STCs were similar when based on absorbed power; cochlear mechanics substantially mature in full-term infants
Evidence_Quote: occurs at a stimulus frequency of 6 kHz

Title: Developmental changes in ultrasonic vocalizations by infant Japanese echolocating bats, Pipistrellus abramus.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: Japanese house bat (Pipistrellus abramus) pups and adults
Stimulus_Type: natural ultrasonic vocalizations (echolocation precursors and isolation calls)
Outcome: pup vocalizations were frequency-modulated ultrasounds; two call types showed separate developmental patterns
Evidence_Quote: frequency-modulated ultrasounds from 30.0 ± 4.0 kHz to 19.3 ± 1.9 kHz

Title: Postnatal development of 2f1-f2 otoacoustic emissions in pigmented rat.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: distortion-product otoacoustic emissions (primary tones)
Outcome: emissions first detected on postnatal day 14 at 5.7-11.3 kHz; high- to mid-frequency responses matured earlier
Evidence_Quote: The geometric-mean frequencies of the primaries were tested at one-half octave intervals, between 4 and 11.3 kHz

Title: Perception of the pitch of unresolved harmonics by 3- and 7-month-old human infants.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: unresolved harmonic complexes (missing fundamental), bandpass filtered, with pink noise
Outcome: infants categorized complexes by missing-fundamental pitch, indicating discrimination of unresolved harmonics by 3 months
Evidence_Quote: Stimuli were MF complexes bandpass filtered with a -12 dB/octave slope, combined in random phase, presented at 70 dB sound pressure level (SPL) for 650 ms with a 50 ms rise/fall with a pink noise at 65 dB SPL. The conditions were (1) "LOW" unresolved harmonics (2500-4500 Hz) based on MFs of 160 and 200 Hz and (2) "HIGH" unresolved harmonics (4000-6000 Hz) based on MFs of 190 and 200

Title: Induction of single-sided deafness in the newborn rat and its consequence for cochlear nucleus volume development.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: newborn rats (operated postnatal day 10), tested as young adults
Stimulus_Type: intracochlear neomycin (single-sided deafness induction); ABR thresholds
Outcome: ventral cochlear nucleus volume on the deaf side was reduced to 57% of the normal-hearing side
Evidence_Quote: Monaural deafening was considered successful when the hearing threshold was at least 95

Title: Heterogeneity of vocal sac inflation patterns in Odorrana tormota plays a role in call diversity.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: natural vocalizations (eight call types), audio/video recording
Outcome: vocal sac inflation pattern depended on call duration and fundamental frequency
Evidence_Quote: those having a fundamental frequency (F0) of >5000 Hz involved inflation of pars lateralis only, whereas those with an F0 of <4000 Hz

Title: Characterizing spontaneous otoacoustic emissions across the human lifespan.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: human subjects from premature birth through the seventh decade (632 subjects)
Stimulus_Type: spontaneous otoacoustic emissions (no stimulus)
Outcome: newborns had more numerous, higher-level and higher-frequency SOAEs than young adults; elderly ears were reduced in level
Evidence_Quote: Newborn SOAEs are also an average of 5 to 6 dB higher

Title: Music reduces pain perception in healthy newborns: A comparison between different music tracks and recoded heartbeat.
Journal: Early human development
Target_Age: healthy full-term newborns aged 1 to 3 days
Stimulus_Type: music (Mozart K.448; Beethoven Moonlight Sonata) and recorded heartbeat sounds
Outcome: music and heartbeat exposure reduced heart rate and pain perception and increased oxygen saturation compared with no music
Evidence_Quote: heartbeat sound recordings (70 bpm) or no music

Title: Yes/no and two-interval forced-choice tasks with listener-based vs observer-based responses.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: 1000-Hz FM tone in quiet; word in two-talker speech masker
Outcome: observer-based thresholds were higher than listener-based; signal-temporal uncertainty accounted for most of the difference
Evidence_Quote: Detection thresholds were estimated adaptively for a 1000-Hz FM tone

Title: The maturation of the central auditory conduction in preterm infants until three months post term. II. The auditory brainstem responses (ABRs).
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: preterm infants (65 infants, followed to 3 months post term)
Stimulus_Type: auditory brainstem responses (ABR)
Outcome: ABR component detectability reached 80-100% at about 32 weeks conceptional age; latencies decreased with maturation
Evidence_Quote: The detectability of the different components in the ABR tests at 70 dB

Title: Infant speech-sound discrimination testing: effects of stimulus intensity and procedural model on measures of performance.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: speech sounds /ba/ vs /da/ (operant head-turn procedure)
Outcome: discrimination performance improved significantly with stimulus intensity; response decrement supported a vigilance model
Evidence_Quote: was measured at three stimulus intensity levels (50, 60, and 70 dB SPL)

Title: Auditory brain stem responses from human adults and infants: restriction of frequency contribution by notched-noise masking.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: click-evoked ABR with notched-noise masking
Outcome: wave V latency and amplitude were similar for adults and infants in the 1.0-kHz notch; differences emerged at higher notch frequencies
Evidence_Quote: Notch center frequencies were set at 1.0, 4.0, and 8.0 kHz. Responses were obtained at 20, 40, and 60 dBnHL

Title: Infants' discrimination of final syllable fundamental frequency in multisyllabic stimuli.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: synthetic multisyllabic speechlike stimuli with final-syllable F0 increments
Outcome: infants discriminated F0 increments of 5-30 Hz above chance; performance did not differ by syllable number
Evidence_Quote: for increments of 10, 20, and 30 Hz relative to a 150-Hz standard

Title: Auditory structure and function in the bird middle ear: an evaluation by SEM and capacitive probe.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: neonatal chick and parakeet (anatomy in five avian species)
Stimulus_Type: acoustic stimulation for tympanic membrane velocity measurement (capacitive probe)
Outcome: tympanic membrane velocity resembled a bandpass filter with best frequency 1.5-3.0 kHz; displacement was linear between 70 and 120 dB SPL
Evidence_Quote: The velocity vs frequency response curve, measured from the tip of the concave tympanic membrane, and corrected to a constant stimulus level of 100 dB SPL, was obtained for the neonatal chick and parakeet for frequencies between 0.2 and 10.0 kHz with a capacitive probe. In both species this curve resembled a bandpass filter whose best frequency was in the range of 1.5-3.0 kHz. The low and high frequency roll-off was 6 and 16 dB per octave, respectively.

Title: Early hearing deprivation by silicon earplugs does not alter electrophysiological development of mouse dorsal cochlear nucleus fusiform neurons.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: early hearing deprivation by silicon earplugs; dorsal cochlear nucleus fusiform neuron electrophysiology
Outcome: fusiform neuron electrophysiological maturation did not differ between earplugged and sham-treated mice
Evidence_Quote: inserting silicon earplugs at P14, elevating auditory thresholds by 30-40 dB

Title: Postpartum survival of mice exposed in utero to ultrasound.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: mice exposed in utero (gestation day 8); neonatal survival assessed
Stimulus_Type: ultrasound exposure (continuous wave, water bath)
Outcome: no credible enhancement of neonatal mortality after in utero ultrasound exposure
Evidence_Quote: to ultrasound at 0.44 W/cm2 (+/- 20%) spatial average intensity, 2 MHz, continuous wave

Title: Fundamental frequency in the speech of infants and children.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: six normal infants and children aged 33 to 169 weeks
Stimulus_Type: speech recordings (narrow-band spectrographic analysis)
Outcome: fundamental frequency values ranged from 30 to 2500 Hz; fry, modal and high registers were discussed
Evidence_Quote: Fundamental frequency values ranged from 30 to 2500 Hz

Title: Acoustic features of infant vocalic utterances at 3, 6, and 9 months.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: infant vocalic utterances (comfort-state recordings)
Outcome: mean f0 was 445 Hz at 3 months, 450 Hz at 6 months and 415 Hz at 9 months; F1 and F2 ranges increased with age
Evidence_Quote: The f0 frequency averaged 445 Hz for 3-month-olds, 450 Hz for 6-month-olds, and 415 Hz for 9-month-olds

Title: Infants require low-frequency energy to hear the pitch of the missing fundamental.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: harmonic tonal complexes (missing fundamental)
Outcome: infants categorized low-frequency (resolvable) complexes by missing-fundamental pitch but failed to categorize high-frequency (unresolvable) complexes
Evidence_Quote: based on missing fundamental frequencies of 160 and 200 Hz

Title: The relationship between auditory brainstem response latencies and behavioral thresholds in normal hearing infants and adults.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: tone pips (ABR latencies and behavioral thresholds)
Outcome: 3-month-olds with higher behavioral thresholds had longer wave V latencies and I-V intervals; no such relation at 6 months or in adults
Evidence_Quote: auditory brainstem response (ABR) latencies for 4 and 8 kHz tone pips

Title: Pressure transfer function and absorption cross section from the diffuse field to the human infant ear canal.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: pink noise in a reverberant diffuse field (ear-canal pressure measurement)
Outcome: ear-canal resonance decreased from 4.4 kHz at 1 month to 2.9 kHz at 24 months; concha resonance decreased from 5.5 to 4.5 kHz
Evidence_Quote: The diffuse-field pressure transfer function from a reverberant field to the ear canal of human infants, ages 1, 3, 6, 12, and 24 months, has been measured from 125-10700 Hz

Title: The growth of hearing loss in neonatal chicks exposed to intense pure tones.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: intense pure tone exposure
Outcome: threshold shift was greatest at 1.3 kHz (maximum loss about 57 dB); tuning sharpness decreased for probe tones above 0.9 kHz
Evidence_Quote: One-day-old chicks were exposed to an intense pure tone (0.9 kHz, 120 dB SPL)

Title: Acoustic impedance of the maternal abdomen.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: nine women in the last trimester of pregnancy
Stimulus_Type: electromechanical shaker (abdominal vibrations)
Outcome: abdominal impedance showed low-frequency compliance, a resonance at 28 ± 16 Hz, and a mass effect at higher frequencies
Evidence_Quote: produced abdominal vibrations between 10 and 500 Hz

Title: Tectorial membrane regeneration in acoustically damaged birds: an immunocytochemical technique.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: octave band noise exposure
Outcome: the tectorial membrane lesion was repaired within 7 days in both chicks and quail
Evidence_Quote: Birds were exposed to an octave band noise with a center frequency of 1.5 kHz at 116 dB SPL for 4 h

Title: Ontogeny of hearing in the marsupial, Monodelphis domestica, as revealed by brainstem auditory evoked potentials.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: brainstem auditory evoked potentials (tone stimuli)
Outcome: hearing onset at postnatal day 29 with range 5-20 kHz; adult audiogram reached by about day 40
Evidence_Quote: The hearing range at the onset of hearing is limited to 5-20 kHz with lowest thresholds of 60 dB SPL at 8-12 kHz

Title: Distortion product otoacoustic emission suppression tuning curves in human adults and neonates.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: 15 normal-hearing adults and 16 healthy term-born neonates
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE (2f1-f2) iso-suppression tuning curves
Outcome: neonatal STCs at 3000 and 6000 Hz were comparable in shape, width and slope to adult STCs; cochlear tuning mature by term birth
Evidence_Quote: The 2f1-f2 DPOAE was elicited using f2/f1 = 1.2, LI = 1.2, LI = 65 and L2 = 50 dB SPL

Title: Anatomy of the normal human cochlear aqueduct with functional implications.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: human temporal bones, ages 0-100 years (101 bones, 19 aged 0-1 years)
Stimulus_Type: anatomical measurements and quantitative modeling of the cochlear aqueduct
Outcome: the aqueduct filters cardiac- and respiration-induced CSF pulses and has little effect on sound transmission above 20 Hz in normal ears
Evidence_Quote: has little effect on normal ossicular transmission of sound for frequencies above 20 Hz. In pathological ears, such as those with ossicular disruption or after a type IV tympanoplasty, a patent aqueduct might affect hearing for frequencies below 150 Hz.

Title: Infants' pitch perception: masking by low- and high-frequency noises.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: pure tones and harmonic tonal complexes with low- and high-frequency noise maskers
Outcome: both groups discriminated tones in high-frequency noise but not low-frequency noise; complexes were categorized by missing fundamental in low-frequency noise
Evidence_Quote: Adults and infants were presented with either pure tones of 160 and 200 Hz

Title: Gender distinctions and lateral asymmetry in the low-level auditory brainstem response of the human neonate.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: clicks and tone burst stimuli (ABR thresholds)
Outcome: male infants had lower ABR thresholds than females; right-ear wave V amplitude was larger in both sexes
Evidence_Quote: in response to clicks and tone burst stimuli between 500 and 8000 Hz

Title: Forward masking among infant and adult listeners.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: 1000-Hz tone probe; broadband noise forward masker
Outcome: Infants showed more forward masking than adults, especially at short masker-probe intervals
Evidence_Quote: Listeners detected a repeated 1000-Hz probe, with 16-ms rise time, no steady-state duration, and 16-ms fall time. Unmasked thresholds were determined for one group of listeners who were trained to respond when they heard the probe but not at other times. In the masking conditions, each tone burst was preceded by a 100-ms broadband noise masker at 65 dB SPL

Title: Basic properties of the sound-evoked post-auricular muscle response (PAMR).
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: human subjects incl. very young infants (ages not specified)
Stimulus_Type: click and tone-burst stimuli (post-auricular muscle response)
Outcome: PAMR basic properties described; infant responses reach adult values by 12 months
Evidence_Quote: It can be obtained with click and tone-burst stimuli within 20 dB of the subjective detection threshold, can be evoked with tone-bursts between 500 Hz and 16 kHz and grows either linearly with the click level or approximately exponentially with the tone-burst level, reaching a maximum of as large as 250 microV pp in some subjects. It has a frequency spectrum mostly between 25 and 200 Hz.

Title: Infants' sensitivity to broadband noise.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: 1000-Hz tone and broadband noise
Outcome: Infant-adult threshold differences smaller for broadband noise than for tones
Evidence_Quote: Unmasked and masked thresholds for a 1000-Hz tone and for broadband noise were estimated adaptively for infants and adults using an observer-based behavioral procedure.

Title: Maturation of cochlear nonlinearity as measured by distortion product otoacoustic emission suppression growth in humans.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: adults, children, term-born and premature neonates
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE primary tones with suppressor tones
Outcome: Neonates showed shallower suppression growth and elevated suppression thresholds for low-frequency suppressors
Evidence_Quote: DPOAE suppression growth was measured at two f2 frequencies (1500 and 6000 Hz) and three primary tone levels (55-45, 65-55, and 75-65 dB SPL).

Title: Development of f2/f1 ratio functions in humans.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: pre-term infants, term infants, and young adults
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE primary tones (f2/f1 ratio functions)
Outcome: Optimal f2/f1 ratio and Q3 showed age x frequency interactions; cochlear mechanisms still maturing at term
Evidence_Quote: Frequency ratio functions were analyzed at three f2 frequencies--2000, 4000 and 6000 Hz.

Title: Middle ear development. I: Extra-stapedius response in the neonatal chick.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: sound stimuli (extra-stapedius velocity by laser interferometry)
Outcome: Low-frequency sensitivity increased by 11 dB with age; no consistent high-frequency improvement
Evidence_Quote: The ES velocity and phase responses in the frequency range between 0.2 and 10.0 kHz were measured in animals ranging from 3 days of age to adult.

Title: Influence of swaddling on sleep and arousal characteristics of healthy infants.
Journal: Pediatrics
Stimulus_Type: white noise of increasing intensity (arousal threshold test)
Outcome: Swaddling increased sleep efficiency, but lower-intensity stimuli induced cortical arousals during REM sleep
Evidence_Quote: In both conditions, the infants were exposed to white noise of increasing intensity, from 50 to 100 dB(A), during rapid eye movement sleep, to determine their arousal thresholds.

Title: Maturation of the cortical auditory evoked potential in infants and young children.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: newborns (<7 days), toddlers (13-41 months), children (4-6 years), adults (18-45 years)
Stimulus_Type: 400 Hz and 3000 Hz tones and word token /baed/
Outcome: CAEP component latencies and amplitudes mature from birth to adulthood
Evidence_Quote: CAEPs were obtained in response to low (400 Hz) and high (3000 Hz) tones and to the word token /baed/, all presented at 60 dB HL, at a rate of 0.22 Hz.

Title: Theory of forward and reverse middle-ear transmission applied to otoacoustic emissions in infant and adult ears.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: no new subjects (theory; prior data from infants through 6 months and adults)
Stimulus_Type: none (scattering-matrix model of middle-ear transmission)
Outcome: Larger infant DPOAE levels attributed mainly to reverse middle-ear transmittance varying with ear-canal area
Evidence_Quote: In a previous study, distortion product (DP) OAE input/output (I/O) functions were shown to differ at f2 = 6 kHz in adults compared to infants through 6 months of age.

Title: In vivo ultrasonic attenuation slope estimates for detecting cervical ripening in rats: Preliminary results.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: rats (pregnant, in vivo; ex vivo cervix)
Stimulus_Type: 33-MHz focused ultrasound (attenuation slope estimation)
Outcome: No significant effect of ultrasonic attenuation with gestational age in vivo
Evidence_Quote: Spherically-focused f/3 transducers with 33-MHz center frequencies and with 9-mm focal lengths were used in both the simulations and experiments.

Title: Effects of maturation on tympanometric wideband acoustic transfer functions in human infants.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: wideband acoustic transfer function measurements at varying static ear-canal pressures
Outcome: Energy reflectance and admittance showed frequency-dependent developmental changes with ear-canal pressure
Evidence_Quote: For frequencies from 0.25 to 0.75 kHz there was as much as a 30% change in mean ER and mid |Y| with changes in static ear-canal pressure between 4 and 24 weeks of age. From 0.75 to 2 kHz, the effects of pressure produced a small number of significant differences in ER and mid |Y| with age, suggestive of a developmentally stable frequency range. Between 2 and 6 kHz, there were differential effects of pressure for the youngest infants; negative pressures caused increased ER and mid |Y| and positive pressures caused decreased ER and mid |Y|; the magnitude of this effect decreased with age.

Title: Methods for estimating infant thresholds.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: 1000-Hz, 16-ms tone bursts
Outcome: Thresholds similar across estimation techniques; constant stimuli least variable
Evidence_Quote: Detection thresholds for 1000-Hz, 16-ms tone bursts were estimated for 3- and 6-month-old infants and for young adults.

Title: Auditory processing during sleep in preterm infants: An event related potential study.
Journal: Early human development
Target_Age: premature infants (mean GA 30 weeks; post-conceptional age 35 weeks)
Stimulus_Type: oddball tones: standard 1000 Hz, deviant 2000 Hz
Outcome: Deviant-tone frontal negativity (200-300 ms) present only in active sleep
Evidence_Quote: frequently occurring 'standard' tones at 1000Hz and infrequent 'deviant' tones at 2000Hz.

Title: Six-month-old infants discriminate voicing on the basis of temporal envelope cues (L).
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: speech tokens /aba/ and /apa/ with envelope information below 64 Hz
Outcome: Infants discriminated voicing from temporal envelope cues alone
Evidence_Quote: processed to retain envelope information below 64 Hz while degrading temporal fine structure cues.

Title: Increased heating by diagnostic ultrasound due to nonlinear propagation.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: 3.6-MHz focused ultrasound
Outcome: Nonlinear propagation enhanced heating (up to about 3x); maximum temperature rise 2 degrees C
Evidence_Quote: Measurements were made of the temperature rise in a sample of tissue-mimicking gel, caused by the application of 3.6-MHz focused ultrasonic beams for 3 min.

Title: Perception of missing fundamental pitch by 3- and 4-month-old human infants.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: missing-fundamental harmonic complexes; masking noise; bandpass filtering
Outcome: Infants categorized complexes by missing-fundamental pitch
Evidence_Quote: This study investigated the ability of 3- and 4-month-olds to perceive the pitch of MF harmonic complexes based on fundamentals of 160 Hz and 200 Hz using an observer-based method. In experiment I, to demonstrate MF pitch discrimination, 3- and 4-month-olds were required to ignore spectral changes in complexes with the same fundamental and to respond only when the fundamental changed. In experiment II, a 60-260 Hz noise was presented with complexes to mask combination tones at the fundamental frequency. In experiment III, complexes were bandpass filtered with a -12 dB/octave slope to limit use of spectral edge cues and presented with a pink noise to mask all distortion products.

Title: Preliminary evaluation of a two-interval, two-alternative infant behavioral testing procedure.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: noise band (detection task)
Outcome: Two-interval forced-choice procedure feasible and efficient in infants
Evidence_Quote: Ten of 11 infants (7-9 months of age) achieved a criterion of 80%-correct detection of a 50-dB sound pressure level noise band in a single testing session.

Title: Modified spectral tilt affects infants' native-language discrimination of approximants and vowels.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: speech sounds /r/-/l/ and vowels with spectral tilt
Outcome: 6-month-olds discriminated spectrally modified sounds; 9-month-olds only unmodified
Evidence_Quote: Infants were presented with /r/-/l/ and /ɔ/-/ɐ/ in three conditions: (a) unmodified; (b) -6 dB/octave tilt; and (c) +6 dB/octave tilt.

Title: Discrimination of frequency transitions by human infants.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: 1.0-kHz pulsed-tone standard with linear frequency transitions
Outcome: Frequency-sweep DLs about 3-4%; brief sweeps harder to discriminate
Evidence_Quote: Difference limens (DLs) for linear frequency transitions using a 1.0-kHz pulsed-tone standard were obtained from 6- to 9-month-old human infants in a series of three experiments.

Title: Phonetic enhancement of Mandarin vowels and tones: Infant-directed speech and Lombard speech.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: eight-talker babble noise (Lombard speech condition)
Outcome: Vowel space expanded in IDS and Lombard speech; tone space expansion only in IDS
Evidence_Quote: Vowel and tone productions were produced by 15 Mandarin-speaking mothers during interactions with their 12-month-old infants during a play session (IDS), in conversation with a Mandarin-speaking adult in a 70 dBA eight-talker babble noise environment (Lombard speech), and in a quiet environment (adult-directed speech).

Title: Ontogeny of auditory brainstem responses in the bat, Phyllostomus discolor.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: bats (Phyllostomus discolor), juveniles (p7 to p200) and adults
Stimulus_Type: clicks and narrowband tone pips (ABR)
Outcome: Juveniles responsive up to 90 kHz by p7; hearing sensitivity increases until about p14
Evidence_Quote: measured auditory brainstem responses (ABRs) to clicks and narrowband tone pips covering a large frequency range (5-90 kHz) in juveniles (p7 to p200) and adults of the bat, Phyllostomus discolor.

Title: The influence of developmental noise exposure on the temporal processing of acoustical signals in the auditory cortex of rats.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: Long Evans rats (exposed on postnatal day 14)
Stimulus_Type: broad-band noise exposure
Outcome: Developmental noise exposure permanently altered temporal and rate coding in auditory cortex
Evidence_Quote: The animals were exposed on postnatal day 14 (P14) for 12 minutes to a loud (125 dB SPL) broad-band noise.

Title: Auditory brain stem responses from human adults and infants: wave V tuning curves.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: third-octave-filtered click probes with tonal maskers
Outcome: Infant wave V tuning curves broader (smaller tip-to-tail, lower Q10) for high-frequency probes
Evidence_Quote: Probe stimuli were 1.0, 4.0, and 8.0-kHz third-octave-filtered clicks.

Title: Level and age effects in infant frequency discrimination.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: pure tones at 40 and 80 dB sensation level
Outcome: Infant FDLs worse than adults except at 4000 Hz for 6- and 12-month-olds
Evidence_Quote: Frequency difference limens (FDLs) were estimated for 3-, 6-, and 12-month-old infants and for adults using pure tones at 500, 1000, and 4000 Hz. Each listener provided an FDL at 40 dB and at a higher (80 dB, in most cases) sensation level (SL).

Title: Neural processing of auditory temporal modulations in awake infants.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: awake infants (3 and 10 months) and young adults
Stimulus_Type: amplitude-modulated stimuli (AMFR)
Outcome: AMFR observable at 8 Hz at all ages; reliable 40 Hz responses only in adults
Evidence_Quote: in awake infants (3- and 10-month-olds) and awake young adults and for both slow and faster modulation rates (8 and 40 Hz).

Title: Infant pitch perception: evidence for responding to pitch categories and the missing fundamental.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: harmonic tonal complexes (pitch categories)
Outcome: Infants showed perceptual constancy and missing-fundamental pitch perception
Evidence_Quote: demonstrated the ability to discriminate harmonic complexes from two pitch categories that differed in pitch by approximately 20% (e.g., 160 vs 200 Hz).

Title: TRPA1 deficiency affects cochlear potentials days after noise exposure.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: clicks and 8 kHz tone bursts (ABR); noise exposure
Outcome: TRPA1 deficiency altered summating potentials and rCM after noise exposure
Evidence_Quote: mice exhibited a direct current (DC) shift in the rCM elicited by an 8 kHz tone burst as the sound intensity increased, which was delayed in Trpa1-/- mice.

Title: Binaural interactions in cortical area AI of cats reared with unilateral atresia of the external ear canal.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: adult cats reared with unilateral ear-canal atresia
Stimulus_Type: tones via sealed calibrated acoustic system (no numeric values stated)
Outcome: Binaural interaction classes normal; IID sensitivity shifted for the atretic ear

Title: Frequency and age-dependent auditory evoked potential thresholds in infants.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: tone pips (evoked-potential thresholds)
Outcome: Largest infant-adult threshold difference at 4.0 kHz, decreasing with age
Evidence_Quote: Auditory evoked-potential thresholds to 0.5, 4.0 and 10.0 kHz tone pips were measured in 40 normal infants 2-28 wks old and 14 normal hearing adults. Thresholds to 500 Hz tone pips were based upon the steady-state, 40 Hz evoked potential.

Title: Infants' discrimination of intensity variation in multisyllabic stimuli.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: synthetic CVC syllables with peak-intensity increments
Outcome: Infants discriminated intensity increments of 2 dB and above; better in bisyllabic context
Evidence_Quote: Discrimination performance was above chance for a 2-dB increment, and improved for 4- and 6-dB increments.

Title: Infants' pitch perception: inharmonic tonal complexes.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: harmonic and inharmonic tonal complexes (missing fundamental)
Outcome: Infants discriminated pitch of inharmonic complexes; performance fell with stronger inharmonicity
Evidence_Quote: infants demonstrated the ability to discriminate two harmonic complexes based on missing fundamental frequencies of 160 and 200 Hz.

Title: The development of frequency resolution in humans as revealed by the auditory brain-stem response recorded with notched-noise masking.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: tone pips with notched-noise masking
Outcome: Tuning adultlike by 6 months; 3-month-olds immature at 8000 Hz
Evidence_Quote: Tone-pip stimuli at 1000, 4000, and 8000 Hz (50 dB nHL) were presented simultaneously with notched-noise masking centered at frequencies related to the tone-pip frequency (1/3-oct intervals above and below the probe frequency).

Title: Noise induced hearing loss in fetal sheep.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: broadband noise exposure; clicks and tone bursts via bone oscillator
Outcome: Noise exposure temporarily elevated fetal ABR thresholds by an average of 8 dB
Evidence_Quote: The auditory brainstem response (ABR) was recorded in utero from chronically instrumented fetal sheep prior to and following exposure of pregnant ewes to intense broadband noise (120 dB SPL for 16 h). ABRs were elicited by clicks and tone bursts (0.5, 1, 2, and 4 kHz) delivered through a bone oscillator secured to the fetal skull.

Title: Aspects of spontaneous otoacoustic emissions in healthy newborns.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: spontaneous otoacoustic emissions (no presented stimulus)
Outcome: SOAE prevalence 78%; levels between -2 and 42 dB SPL; most emissions above 2 kHz
Evidence_Quote: The SOAE levels were between -2 and 42 dB SPL. The mean level per emitting ear was 8.0 dB SPL and not significantly different between right and left ears or genders. However, the level of the strongest emission per emitting ear was significantly higher for right than for left ears. In contrast with adults most of the emissions (70%) are at frequencies above 2 kHz.

Title: Simultaneous masking in newborn chickens.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: masker tone with signal tones
Outcome: Simultaneous masking patterns mature at hatching; no developmental change
Evidence_Quote: In the first experiment data were collected with a 500-Hz masker presented at 15 or 25 dB above absolute threshold.

Title: The relationship between auditory brainstem response and behavioral thresholds in normal hearing infants and adults.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: tone pips (ABR and behavioral thresholds)
Outcome: Infant ABR thresholds adultlike at all frequencies; behavioral thresholds elevated relative to adults
Evidence_Quote: Thresholds were estimated for tone pips at 1, 4, and 8 kHz, presented at a rate of 13.3/s.

Title: Decreased cardiac responses to auditory stimulation during prone sleep.
Journal: Pediatrics
Stimulus_Type: white noise during REM sleep
Outcome: Prone sleep decreased cardiac responses to auditory stimulation
Evidence_Quote: Their behavioral and cardiac responses were recorded during rapid eye movement (REM) sleep, both before and after exposure to 90 dB (A) of white-noise.

Title: The cochlear place-frequency map of the adult and developing Mongolian gerbil.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: Mongolian gerbils (adult and subadult, 18 days after birth)
Stimulus_Type: tones for single auditory-nerve-fiber characterization
Outcome: Cochlear place-frequency map established; slope 1.5 mm/octave; map shifts during maturation
Evidence_Quote: The map was established for frequencies between 0.3 and 31.9 kHz.

Title: Distortion product otoacoustic emission (2f1-f2) amplitude as a function of f2/f1 frequency ratio and primary tone level separation in human adults and neonates.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE primary tones (f2/f1 ratio functions)
Outcome: Optimal f2/f1 ratio comparable in adults and neonates; level-separation effects differed for premature neonates
Evidence_Quote: Two f2 frequencies were investigated: 1500 and 6000 Hz.

Title: Features of the auditory development of the short-tailed Brazilian opossum, Monodelphis domestica: evoked responses, neonatal vocalizations and synapses in the inferior colliculus.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: click stimuli; pup isolation calls
Outcome: Hearing onset at postnatal day 24 (threshold 83 dB SPL), declining to below 58 dB by day 40
Evidence_Quote: Evoked potentials were first recorded at postnatal day 24 at a threshold of 83 dB SPL; thresholds declined over subsequent weeks to below 58 dB at 40 days. Isolation calls emitted by the pups had stereotypic spectra with peaks at near 13 kHz and an octave higher.

Title: Distortion product otoacoustic emissions in human newborns and adults. I. Frequency effects.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: human newborns (term and preterm) and adults
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE primary tones (varied stimulus frequency)
Outcome: Newborn 2f1-f2 DPOAE amplitudes larger than adults at lower frequencies
Evidence_Quote: At the highest frequencies assessed (f2 = 4.2-9.9 kHz) all subjects had similar amplitude 2 f1-f2 DPOAEs. At lower frequencies adult 2 f1-f2 amplitudes were significantly less than those of newborns. At the lowest frequencies reliably assessed (f2 = 1.5-2.1 kHz) term newborns had significantly larger 2 f1-f2 DPOAEs than preterm newborns.

Title: Postnatal development of the organ of Corti in cats: a light microscopic morphometric study.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: kittens (P1, P5, P10, P15) and adult cats
Stimulus_Type: none (light-microscopic morphometry; cochlear locations by adult best frequency)
Outcome: Postnatal development of organ of Corti morphology characterized
Evidence_Quote: Measurements were made of the organ of Corti at 3 cochlear locations: 20%, 60% and 85% of basilar membrane length from the base cochlear locations which in the adult correspond to best frequencies of approximately 20 kHz, 2 kHz and 500 Hz, respectively.

Title: Cisplatin ototoxicity in developing gerbils.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: young gerbils (2 weeks of age at first exposure)
Stimulus_Type: cisplatin doses (one to three 5 mg/kg doses)
Outcome: DPOAE amplitude and ABR threshold elevation by cisplatin dose
Evidence_Quote: A tendency for a bimodal distribution of DPOAE and ABR responses was also observed in the D1 group, at frequencies below 8 kHz.

Title: Moderate noise trauma in juvenile cats results in profound cortical topographic map changes in adulthood.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: loud 6 kHz pure-tone exposure
Outcome: reorganization of the auditory cortex frequency map
Evidence_Quote: The present study demonstrates that exposure of 5-week-old kittens to a loud 6 kHz tone, producing mild to moderate high-frequency hearing loss, induces a profound reorganization of the frequency map in auditory cortex.

Title: Gender differences among newborns on a transient otoacoustic emissions test for hearing.
Journal: Journal of music therapy
Target_Age: healthy full-term newborns (38-42 weeks gestation), first 48 hours of life
Stimulus_Type: transient evoked otoacoustic emission (TEOAE) click stimulus
Outcome: gender and frequency differences in TEOAE responses (cochlear sensitivity)
Evidence_Quote: During this test, a sudden burst of sound is presented at between 78 and 83 dB SPL which stimulates the entire basilar membrane.

Title: Binaural masking level differences in infants with and without otitis media with effusion.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: infants aged 7-10 months (with or without otitis media with effusion)
Stimulus_Type: 500 Hz tone signal against narrowband noise masker (binaural masking)
Outcome: masked thresholds and binaural masking level differences
Evidence_Quote: Subjects were trained to detect a 500 Hz signal (either in or out-of-phase between the ears) against an in-phase, narrow band noise masker centred at 500 Hz.

Title: Middle ear and cochlear disorders result in different DPOAE growth behaviour: implications for the differentiation of sound conductive and cochlear hearing loss.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE primary tones (f2 between 2.0 and 8.0 kHz)
Outcome: DPOAE I/O-function growth behaviour in middle-ear vs cochlear disorders
Evidence_Quote: DPOAE I/O-functions were recorded in a wide primary tone level range at up to 8 f2 frequencies between 2.0 and 8.0 kHz (15 dB SPL < L2< 60 dB SPL; L1=0.46 L2 + 41 dB SPL; f2/f1=1.2) in guinea pigs

Title: Prevalence of spontaneous otoacoustic emissions in neonates.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: spontaneous otoacoustic emissions (SOAE) recording
Outcome: SOAE prevalence, frequency ranges and average levels
Evidence_Quote: The majority of adult SOAEs are between 1.0 and 2.0 kHz, whereas the majority of neonatal SOAEs are between 2.5 and 5.0 kHz. The average SOAE level is -2.6 dB SPL for adults and 8.5 dB SPL for infants.

Title: Distortion product otoacoustic emissions for hearing threshold estimation and differentiation between middle-ear and cochlear disorders in neonates.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: neonates (mean age 3.2 days; follow-up at 4 weeks)
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE primary tones (11 test frequencies, f2 = 1.5-8 kHz)
Outcome: hearing threshold estimation; differentiation of middle-ear vs cochlear disorders
Evidence_Quote: DPOAEs were measured in neonates after birth (mean age = 3.2 days) and 4 weeks later (follow-up) at 11 test frequencies between f2 = 1.5 and 8 kHz and compared to that found in normal hearing subjects and cochlear hearing loss patients.

Title: A retrospective study of the spectral probability of spontaneous otoacoustic emissions: rise of octave shifted second mode after infancy.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: neonates, children (5-11 y) and adults (296 subjects across three surveys)
Stimulus_Type: spontaneous otoacoustic emission (SOAE) recordings
Outcome: SOAE frequency distribution (spectral probability) by age group
Evidence_Quote: Neonates show a monomodal distribution with a peak at 4 kHz, but both children (5-11 y) and adults show an identical bimodal distribution, with two peaks in an octave distance (1.5 and 3 kHz).

Title: Noise in contemporary neonatal intensive care.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: no human subjects (sound surveys in two neonatal intensive care units)
Stimulus_Type: NICU ambient sound (weekly sound surveys)
Outcome: equivalent sound pressure levels (LEQ) compared with recommended limits
Evidence_Quote: Median weekly equivalent sound pressure levels (LEQ) for NICU A ranged from 61 to 63 dB (A weighted), depending on the level of care. NICU B L(EQ) measurements ranged from 55 to 60 dB (A weighted).

Title: Pure-tone overstimulation protects surviving avian hair cells from acoustic trauma.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: intense pure-tone exposures (1.5 kHz and 2.2 kHz at 124 dB SPL)
Outcome: hair cell and tectorial membrane damage; protection from second exposure
Evidence_Quote: Chicks were exposed to a pure-tone of 1.5 kHz at 124 dB SPL. Lesion was found in both TM and hair cells, but the area of damage to the TM was much larger than that to the hair cells. Following this exposure, chicks were exposed to a second intense pure-tone at 2.2 kHz 124 dB SPL.

Title: Effects of temporal uncertainty and temporal expectancy on infants' auditory sensitivity.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: 1 kHz tone in broadband noise (with/without acoustic cue)
Outcome: masked detection sensitivity under temporal uncertainty/expectancy
Evidence_Quote: In the present experiment, the effects of temporal uncertainty and temporal expectancy on infants' and adults' detection of a 1 kHz tone in a broadband noise were examined.

Title: The effect of decibel level of music stimuli and gender on head circumference and physiological responses of premature infants in the NICU.
Journal: Journal of music therapy
Target_Age: premature infants in the NICU (gestational ages 28-33 weeks)
Stimulus_Type: lullaby and classical music presented at 65, 70 or 75 dB
Outcome: head circumference growth; heart rate, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation
Evidence_Quote: One quarter of the males and one quarter of the females listened to music presented at an average of 65 dB, one quarter at an average of 70 dB, one quarter at an average of 75 dB, and one quarter did not listen to any music and served as control subjects.

Title: Neuronal responses in chinchilla auditory cortex after postnatal exposure to frequency-modulated tones.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: newborn chinchilla pups (exposure 4 weeks; tested at P28)
Stimulus_Type: continuous upward linear FM sweep exposure (0.1-20 kHz)
Outcome: cortical neuronal responses to pure tones and FM sweeps
Evidence_Quote: Newborn chinchilla pups were exposed continuously to an upward linear FM sweep (0.1-20 kHz) at 0.05 kHz/ms for 4 weeks.

Title: The breaking of cochlear scaling symmetry in human newborns and adults.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE swept-tone protocol (0.5 to 4 kHz segments)
Outcome: DPOAE phase-frequency functions; breaking of cochlear scaling symmetry
Evidence_Quote: In this study, DPOAE phase was recorded with a swept-tone protocol in three, octave-wide segments from 0.5 to 4 kHz.

Title: Processing simultaneous auditory objects: infants' ability to detect mistuning in harmonic complexes.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: harmonic complex tone (240 Hz fundamental, third harmonic mistuned)
Outcome: discrimination of mistuned harmonic complex (auditory object segregation)
Evidence_Quote: The present study used a conditioned head-turn procedure to examine whether 6-month-old infants are able to discriminate a complex tone (240 Hz, 500 ms, six harmonics in random phase with a 6 dB roll-off per octave) from a version with the third harmonic mistuned.

Title: Maturation of the human medial efferent reflex revisited.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: premature and term-born neonates, 6-month-old infants, young adults
Stimulus_Type: contralateral acoustic stimulation (CAS) during DPOAE recording
Outcome: MOC reflex strength (DPOAE amplitude/phase shifts) by age
Evidence_Quote: For all ages, the MOC reflex was strongest at frequencies below 1.5 kHz, and the reflection component of the DPOAE was most affected, showing maximally reduced amplitude and shallower phase slope when contralateral noise was presented.

Title: Distortion-product otoacoustic emission reflection-component delays and cochlear tuning: estimates from across the human lifespan.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: 184 subjects from prematurely born neonates to elderly adults
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE (2f1-f2) recording, 0.5-4 kHz (extended to 8 kHz in young adults)
Outcome: reflection-component delays and cochlear tuning estimates across the lifespan
Evidence_Quote: Distortion product otoacoustic emissions (DPOAEs) at 2f1-f2 were recorded, and their reflection components were extracted in 184 subjects ranging in age from prematurely born neonates to elderly adults. DPOAEs were measured from 0.5-4 kHz in all age groups and extended to 8 kHz in young adults.

Title: Procedures for ambient-pressure and tympanometric tests of aural acoustic reflectance and admittance in human infants and adults.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: human adults and infants (1 month of age)
Stimulus_Type: aural acoustic reflectance and admittance measurement (0.2 to 8 kHz)
Outcome: reflectance/admittance measurement procedures and illustrative normal-ear data
Evidence_Quote: Procedures are described to measure acoustic reflectance and admittance in human adult and infant ears at frequencies from 0.2 to 8 kHz.

Title: Recovery of auditory function following intense sound exposure in the neonatal chick.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: intense pure-tone exposure (0.9 kHz at 120 dB for 48 h)
Outcome: recovery of auditory thresholds and frequency selectivity (Q10 dB)
Evidence_Quote: One day old chicks were exposed to a 0.9 kHz tone for 48 h at 120 dB.

Title: Cortical plasticity with bimodal hearing in children with asymmetric hearing loss.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: children with asymmetric hearing loss (implanted at 8.7 +/- 5.1 years)
Stimulus_Type: monaural acoustic click trains / biphasic electric pulses via cochlear implant
Outcome: cortical lateralization and aural preference; reversal with implant use
Evidence_Quote: Monaurally presented stimuli consisted of 36 ms trains of 9 acoustic clicks/biphasic electric pulses at a rate of 250 Hz, repeated at 1 Hz.

Title: Amplitude modulation detection and temporal modulation cutoff frequency in normal hearing infants.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: three-month-old infants and young adults (normal hearing)
Stimulus_Type: amplitude-modulated broadband noise
Outcome: modulation detection threshold (MDT) and temporal modulation cutoff frequency
Evidence_Quote: The modulation detection threshold (MDT) of a broadband noise amplitude modulated at 10 Hz estimated the y-intercept of the TMTF. The cutoff frequency of the TMTF, measured at a modulation depth 4 dB greater than the MDT, provided an estimate of temporal resolution.

Title: Context matters: Cortical rhythms in infants across baseline and play.
Journal: Infant behavior & development
Stimulus_Type: dynamic audiovisual display (baseline) and object play with mother; EEG recording
Outcome: EEG theta, alpha, beta and gamma power by context and scalp site
Evidence_Quote: Theta (3-6 Hz) and alpha (6-9 Hz) power were higher at frontal sites (Fp1/Fp2) during play relative to baseline. Beta (9-30 Hz) and gamma (30-50 Hz) power were higher at frontal (Fp1/Fp2) and frontal medial sites (F3/F4) during baseline relative to play.

Title: Acoustic analyses of infant fricative and trill vocalizations.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: infant fricative and trill vocalizations (recorded)
Outcome: spectral components and trill rates of infant closants
Evidence_Quote: Closants, or consonantlike sounds in infant vocalizations, were described acoustically using 16-kHz spectrograms and LPC or FFT analyses based on waveforms sampled at 20 or 40 kHz.

Title: Effects of an enhanced acoustic environment on residual hearing following chronic cochlear implantation and electrical stimulation in the partially deafened cat.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: enhanced acoustic environment: 80 dB SPL 4-talker babble, 14 h per day
Outcome: auditory thresholds and cochlear histology after chronic implantation and electrical stimulation
Evidence_Quote: To simulate potential over stimulation via a hearing aid, one cohort of animals were also exposed to an enhanced acoustic environment consisting of 80 dB SPL 4-talker babble presented 14 h per day.

Title: Changes in middle-ear input admittance during postnatal auditory development in chicks.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: sound pressure measurements at the tympanic membrane (7 frequencies, 0.66-1.8 kHz)
Outcome: middle-ear input admittance magnitude and angle development
Evidence_Quote: Admittance at 7 frequencies (0.66-1.8 kHz) was calculated from measurements of the magnitude and phase angle of sound pressure in front of the tympanic membrane.

Title: Maternal vocalisations and other sounds in the fetal lamb's sound environment.
Journal: Early human development
Target_Age: pregnant ewes and fetal lambs (last 3 weeks of gestation)
Stimulus_Type: maternal vocalisations and other sounds recorded in the amniotic sac; playback of ewe bleats
Outcome: attenuation of external sounds across gestation; lamb heart-rate responses to maternal vs alien bleats
Evidence_Quote: Over the last 3 weeks of gestation the attenuation of sounds from outside the mother decreased at frequencies between 500 and 4000 Hz, but not below or above those frequencies.

Title: Age-dependent effects of a pure tone trauma in the chick basilar papilla: evidence for a development of the tonotopic organization.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: chicks and chick embryos (embryonic days 18/20; post-hatch days 1-30)
Stimulus_Type: 1.5 kHz pure tone at 125 dB SPL for 12 h
Outcome: frequency of maximum threshold elevation; basilar papilla damage position
Evidence_Quote: 58 chicks or chick embryos were continuously exposed during 12 h on either embryonic day 18 or 20 or on post-hatching days 1, 10, 20 or 30 to 1.5 kHz pure tone at an intensity of 125 dB SPL.

Title: Consistency and variability in pitch and tempo in infants' everyday musical lives.
Journal: Infant behavior & development
Stimulus_Type: live song renditions by singers in the infant's environment
Outcome: consistency and variability of starting tonic pitches and average tempos
Evidence_Quote: singing a pop song 30 bpm and six semitones apart)

Title: Maturational and degenerative processes in the organ of Corti after neonatal hypothyroidism.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: rats (propylthiouracil during first 30 days after birth)
Stimulus_Type: neonatal hypothyroidism (PTU); BAER and electrocochleography testing
Outcome: elevated auditory thresholds; organ of Corti maturation and degeneration
Evidence_Quote: Maturation of auditory potentials was achieved within 10-15 days but was incomplete since the animals definitely demonstrated elevated thresholds around 60-70 dB SPL.

Title: Acoustical properties of the human skull.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: human skull specimens (fresh and formalin-immersed; no living subjects)
Stimulus_Type: focused ultrasound beam transmitted through skull sections
Outcome: insertion loss, reflection loss and sound speed of the skull
Evidence_Quote: Measurements were made in the frequency range from 0.25 to 6 MHz. Most studies were restricted to an upper frequency limit of 2.2 MHz.

Title: Filtering and spectral characteristics of averaged auditory brain-stem response and background noise in infants.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: clicks and 500-Hz tone bursts for ABR; 30-Hz vs 100-Hz high-pass recording filters
Outcome: ABR amplitude and Fsp; spectra of averaged ABR and background noise
Evidence_Quote: This study compares the effects of 30- and 100-Hz high-pass filters on ABR amplitude and response Fsp in full-term infants. Stimuli used to elicit ABRs are moderate- and low-level clicks and 500-Hz tone bursts.

Title: Frequency contribution to the click-evoked auditory brain-stem response in human adults and infants.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: click stimuli with notched-noise masking (center frequencies 500-8000 Hz)
Outcome: ABR wave I and V latency and morphology by masker frequency
Evidence_Quote: Results indicate that 3-month-old infants have adultlike latency shifts (re: unmasked latency) when the ABR is recorded in the presence of notched-noise masking with center frequencies ranging from 500-8000 Hz.

Title: Changes in the cat cochlear nucleus following neonatal deafening and chronic intracochlear electrical stimulation.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: cats (neonatally deafened kittens; implanted at 8-16 weeks)
Stimulus_Type: chronic intracochlear electrical stimulation; ABR and frequency following response testing
Outcome: cochlear nucleus volume, spherical cell area and density
Evidence_Quote: Profound hearing loss was confirmed in each animal by auditory brainstem response (ABR) and frequency following response (500 Hz) testing. Five of the kittens were implanted unilaterally with a scala tympani electrode array at ages 8-16 weeks. These kittens were stimulated daily for four hours at 2 dB above the evoked ABR threshold, over a period of three months

Title: The sensitivity to 3,3'-iminodipropionitrile differs for high- and midfrequency hearing loss in the developing rat.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: developing rats (IDPN exposure gestational day 15 to postnatal day 72; tested as adults)
Stimulus_Type: 5- and 40-kHz tones (reflex modification audiometry); IDPN exposure
Outcome: auditory thresholds; frequency-selective hearing loss by exposure age
Evidence_Quote: All animals were tested as adults for auditory thresholds to 5- and 40-kHz tones using reflex modification audiometry.

Title: Ear-canal impedance and reflection coefficient in human infants and adults.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: infants aged 1, 3, 6, 12 and 24 months, and adults
Stimulus_Type: ear-canal impedance and reflection coefficient measurement (125-10,700 Hz)
Outcome: ear-canal input impedance and reflection coefficient development
Evidence_Quote: The ear-canal impedance and reflection coefficient were measured in an adult group and in groups of infants of age 1, 3, 6, 12, and 24 months over frequency range 125-10,700 Hz.

Title: Amplitude-modulation following response (AMFR): effects of modulation rate, carrier frequency, age, and state.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: amplitude-modulated tones (carriers 500 and 2000 Hz)
Outcome: AMFR coherence; optimal modulation rate by age and state
Evidence_Quote: Stimulus AM rate was varied between 10 and 80 Hz for continuous tonal stimuli of 500 Hz, and between 20 and 80 Hz for continuous tonal stimuli of 2000 Hz.

Title: Coherence analysis of envelope-following responses (EFRs) and frequency-following responses (FFRs) in infants and adults.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: amplitude-modulated tones
Outcome: FFR and EFR coherence growth and thresholds
Evidence_Quote: 'Best frequency' (i.e., infant 80 Hz and adult 40 Hz) EFR thresholds were the same for infants and adults at 500 and 1000 Hz, but infant EFR thresholds were poorer than adult thresholds at 2000 Hz.

Title: Thyroxine affects physiological and morphological development of the ear.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE (DPE) and ABR recording; thyroxine-induced hyperthyroidism
Outcome: onset and maturation of DPEs and ABR thresholds
Evidence_Quote: DPEs were recorded at an earlier postnatal age to high (8 kHz) frequencies and progressed to lower (3 kHz) frequencies with age.

Title: The effect of the evanescent wave upon acoustic measurements in the human ear canal.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: no subjects (theoretical predictions for human ear canals; adults and 1-month-old infants referenced)
Stimulus_Type: acoustic measurement in the ear canal with loudspeaker and microphone (theory)
Outcome: predicted maximum evanescent-wave measurement error
Evidence_Quote: The maximum measurement error due to the presence of the evanescent wave in human ear canals below 10 kHz is predicted to be 3 dB in adults and 1.3 dB in 1 month old infants, when the loudspeaker and microphone ports are spaced more than 2 mm apart.

Title: Cochlear pathology induced by aminoglycoside ototoxicity during postnatal maturation in cats.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: neomycin sulfate (aminoglycoside) administration
Outcome: cochlear hair cell and spiral ganglion degeneration patterns
Evidence_Quote: In contrast, the spiral ganglion exhibited a different pattern of degeneration with initial cell loss occurring in the middle of the cochlea, about 40-60% from the base (approximately 2.8-8 kHz).

Title: Development of auditory function in the tammar wallaby Macropus eugenii.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: tammar wallaby pouch young (95 to >180 days)
Stimulus_Type: click and tone burst stimuli by bone and air conduction (ABR)
Outcome: ABR thresholds and latencies across pouch development
Evidence_Quote: Thresholds to tone bursts in the centre frequency range (4-12 kHz) remained less than those for low (0.5-1.5 kHz) and higher (16 kHz) frequencies.

Title: Development of human cochlear active mechanism asymmetry: involvement of the medial olivocochlear system?
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: pre-term and full-term neonates (73 ears of 49 neonates)
Stimulus_Type: broad band white noise (contralateral stimulation)
Outcome: TEOAE suppression increased with conceptional age; right-ear advantage in older neonates
Evidence_Quote: The continuous contralateral stimulation was a broad band white noise, presented at 70 dB SPL.

Title: The effects of maturation and stimulus parameters on the optimal f(2)/f(1) ratio of the 2f(1)-f(2) distortion product otoacoustic emission in neonates(1).
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: neonates 30-42 weeks conceptional age and adults
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE primary tones (f1-sweep)
Outcome: optimum f2/f1 ratio depends on primary frequency and level; no neonate-adult difference in optimum ratio
Evidence_Quote: The adult group was used to investigate the effect of stimulus level on the optimum f(2)/f(1) ratio for f(2) frequencies from 1.7 to 10 kHz.

Title: DPOAE suppression tuning: cochlear immaturity in premature neonates or auditory aging in normal-hearing adults?
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE primary tones (suppression tuning curves)
Outcome: children's STCs comparable to adults and different from premature neonates
Evidence_Quote: DPOAE STCs were recorded at 1500, 3000, and 6000 Hz using optimal parameters in normal-hearing children and adults.

Title: A longitudinal study of distortion product otoacoustic emission ipsilateral suppression and input/output characteristics in human neonates.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: prematurely born neonates, term-born neonates, and adults
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE primary tones (f2 = 6000 Hz)
Outcome: neonates show narrower suppression tuning than adults; cochlear immaturity persists postnatally
Evidence_Quote: DPOAE suppression and I/O functions for f2 = 6000 Hz were measured in a group of prematurely born neonates at weekly intervals over a period of 7-8-weeks, a group of normal-hearing adults, and during a one-time test session in a group of term-born neonates.

Title: Decreased arousals among healthy infants after short-term sleep deprivation.
Journal: Pediatrics
Target_Age: healthy infants, median age 8 weeks (range 6-18 weeks)
Stimulus_Type: white noise of increasing intensity during REM sleep
Outcome: sleep deprivation increased arousal thresholds and obstructive apnea episodes
Evidence_Quote: the infants were exposed, during rapid eye movement (REM) sleep, to white noise of increasing intensity, from 50 dB(A) to 100 dB(A), to determine their arousal thresholds.

Title: Distortion product otoacoustic emission (2f1-f2) suppression in 3-month-old infants: evidence for postnatal maturation of human cochlear function?
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: premature neonates, term-born neonates, 3-month-old infants, and adults
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE primary tones
Outcome: infants show non-adult-like STC width and suppression growth; postnatal cochlear immaturity
Evidence_Quote: DPOAE suppression tuning curves (STC) and suppression growth patterns were measured in the three age groups at f2 = 6000 Hz, L1 = 65, L2 = 55 dB SPL, with an f2/f1 of 1.2.

Title: The effect of gender on one-day-old infants' behavior and heart rate responses to music decibel level.
Journal: Journal of music therapy
Stimulus_Type: instrumental lullaby music at three loudness levels
Outcome: no significant heart rate or behavior state differences across loudness levels or by gender
Evidence_Quote: played at three different loudness levels: 55-60 dB, 65-70 dB, and 75-80 dB.

Title: Effect of masker-frequency variability on the detection performance of infants and adults.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: 1000-Hz pure tone signal with two-tone complex or broadband noise maskers
Outcome: infants more susceptible to informational masking than adults
Evidence_Quote: Listeners detected a 300-ms 1000-Hz pure tone masked by: (1) A random-frequency two-tone complex; (2) a fixed-frequency two-tone complex; or (3) a broadband noise. Maskers repeated at 300-ms intervals throughout testing at 60 dB SPL.

Title: Distortion product otoacoustic emission suppression tuning and acoustic admittance in human infants: birth through 6 months.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: 20 infants, birth through 6 months of age
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE suppression tuning curves; acoustic admittance/reflectance
Outcome: STCs remained narrow and sharp from birth through 6 months; middle-ear indices changed with age, weakly correlated with suppression
Evidence_Quote: Previous work has reported non-adultlike distortion product otoacoustic emission (DPOAE) suppression in human newborns at f2=6000 Hz, indicating an immaturity in peripheral auditory function.

Title: Maturation of the traveling-wave delay in the human cochlea.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: 227 subjects, 29 weeks conceptional age to 49 years
Stimulus_Type: click stimuli with high-pass noise masking (derived-band ABR)
Outcome: traveling-wave delay between 11.3 and 5.7 kHz bands decreases with age, adult-like by 3-6 months
Evidence_Quote: The derived response technique was applied to ABRs obtained with click stimuli (presented at a fixed level equal to 60-dB sensation level in normal hearing adults) in the presence of high-pass noise masking (slope 96 dB/oct) to obtain frequency specific responses from octave-wide bands.

Title: Chronic intracochlear electrical stimulation induces selective survival of spiral ganglion neurons in neonatally deafened cats.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: neonatally deafened kittens, implanted at 9-17 weeks of age
Stimulus_Type: chronic intracochlear electrical stimulation
Outcome: 3 months of stimulation improved spiral ganglion neuron survival near the electrodes
Evidence_Quote: Profound hearing losses were documented by ABR and FFR (500 Hz) testing. At 9-17 weeks of age, the young deafened cats were unilaterally implanted with a multichannel scala tympani electrode. Six of the animals were chronically stimulated at 6 dB above electrically evoked ABR thresholds for 1 h/day for periods of 1 month or 3 months.

Title: Effect of age at onset of deafness on binaural sensitivity in electric hearing in humans.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: cochlear implant stimulation (ITD/ILD cues)
Outcome: ITD sensitivity retained mainly with adult or late-childhood deafness onset; ILD sensitivity present in all subjects
Evidence_Quote: Sensitivity to interaural timing difference (ITD) and interaural level difference (ILD) cues was measured at basal, middle, and apical pitch-matched places of stimulation along the cochlear arrays, using a stimulation rate of 100 Hz.

Title: Ear and hearing problems in relation to karyotype in children with Turner syndrome.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: 60 children with Turner syndrome, age 1.7-21.2 years
Stimulus_Type: audiometric evaluation (no set acoustic stimulus values)
Outcome: hearing thresholds about 10-11 dB worse in monosomy 45,X or isochromosome karyotypes
Evidence_Quote: Hearing thresholds in general appeared to be about 10-11 dB worse in children with a monosomy 45,X or isochromosome

Title: Frequency shifts with age in click-evoked otoacoustic emissions of preterm infants.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: click-evoked otoacoustic emissions (CEOAEs)
Outcome: CEOAE spectral components shift with postmenstrual age (10 Hz/week around 2 kHz; 30 Hz/week around 4.25 kHz)
Evidence_Quote: with a mean estimate of 10 Hz/week for frequencies around 2 kHz and 30 Hz/week for frequencies around 4.25 kHz.

Title: Infant speech-sound discrimination in noise.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: speech sounds (/ba/ vs /ga/) in noise at varied signal-to-noise ratios
Outcome: infants required greater S/N than adults; threshold difference 5.8 dB S/N favoring adults
Evidence_Quote: testing each infant at four S/N's (-8, 0, 8, and 16 dB). Adults were tested for comparison at four S/N's (-12, -8, -4, and 0 dB).

Title: Development of pitch processing: infants' discrimination of iterated rippled noise stimuli with unresolved spectral content.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: high-pass filtered iterated rippled noise (IRN)
Outcome: infants discriminated F0 change from 167 to 200 Hz only after pitch priming
Evidence_Quote: showed above-chance discrimination of a change from 167 to 200 Hz in the fundamental frequency (F0) of such high-passed filtered IRN stimuli

Title: Stimulus-frequency otoacoustic emissions in human newborns.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: 15 human newborns (adult comparison values from prior reports)
Stimulus_Type: stimulus-frequency otoacoustic emission (SFOAE) probe tones
Outcome: newborn SFOAE delays adult-like when compared at stimulus levels of linear growth
Evidence_Quote: SFOAEs in newborns were measured at stimulus levels as low as 15 dB sound pressure level (SPL).

Title: In vitro ultrasonic heating of fetal bone.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: human fetal femurs in vitro (several gestational ages)
Stimulus_Type: 1 MHz continuous wave ultrasound exposure in vitro
Outcome: temperature increase in fetal bone up to 30 times greater than in soft tissue
Evidence_Quote: The temperature increase measured in vitro in human fetal femurs exposed to 1 MHz, continuous wave ultrasound at 37 degrees C is reported.

Title: Developmental changes in masked thresholds.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: listeners 6.5 months to 20.5 years of age
Stimulus_Type: octave-band noises in broadband masker
Outcome: masked thresholds declined exponentially with age for all stimuli
Evidence_Quote: Masked thresholds for octave-band noises with center frequencies of 0.4, 1, 2, 4, and 10 kHz and for a 1/3-octave-band noise centered at 10 kHz were obtained from listeners 6.5 months to 20.5 years of age at two levels of a broadband masker (0 and 10 dB/cycle).

Title: Fetal auditory evoked responses to onset of amplitude modulated sounds. A fetal magnetoencephalography (fMEG) study.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: fetuses at 31-40 weeks of gestation (55 pregnant women)
Stimulus_Type: amplitude modulated tone (500 Hz carrier) presented to maternal abdomen
Outcome: fetal response latencies shorter for middle and high modulation rates; maturation effect for 4/s
Evidence_Quote: presentation of an amplitude modulated tone (AM) with a carrier frequency of 500 Hz to the maternal abdomen

Title: Pure-tone sensitivity of human infants.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: pure tones
Outcome: infant thresholds 10-30 dB higher than adults, greatest difference at 8000 Hz
Evidence_Quote: Pure-tone thresholds at frequencies ranging from 250 to 8000 Hz were estimated for 3-, 6-, and 12-month-old infants and for adults, using the Observer-based Psychoacoustic Procedure (OPP).

Title: Hearing loss caused by CMV infection is correlated with reduced endocochlear potentials caused by strial damage in murine models.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: neonatal mice (BALB/c and C57BL6), tested at 6-8 weeks
Stimulus_Type: tonal stimuli (ABR)
Outcome: CMV infection caused strial capillary loss, reduced endocochlear potentials, and ABR threshold elevations
Evidence_Quote: At 6 weeks, ABR thresholds to tonal stimuli at 8, 16 and 32 kHz were determined for each ear.

Title: Postnatal development of auditory nerve and cochlear nucleus neuronal responses in kittens.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: acoustic stimuli (auditory nerve and cochlear nucleus recordings)
Outcome: neural thresholds and tuning immature in the first postnatal week, maturing by postnatal day 20
Evidence_Quote: Phase-locking abilities are poor in developing mammals and all neurons exhibit broad bandpass tuning curves, with center frequencies clustering near 1.5 kHz.

Title: Infants' localization of sounds in the median sagittal plane: effects of signal frequency.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: bandpass noise bursts (three spectral conditions)
Outcome: minimum audible angle decreased with age; best performance for the 8-12 kHz signal
Evidence_Quote: For each of three bandpass noise conditions (less than 4 kHz, 4-8 kHz, 8-12 kHz), minimum audible angle (MAA) for each listener, i.e., the smallest of the four angular shifts in vertical sound location that the listener could reliably detect, was estimated.

Title: Masking effects on ABR waves I and V in infants and adults.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: 4-kHz tone pip with high- and low-pass maskers (ABR)
Outcome: masking patterns for ABR waves I and V differ between infants and adults
Evidence_Quote: The signal was a 4-kHz tone pip presented at 86 dB peak equivalent sound-pressure level (p.e.SPL).

Title: Auditory brain stem responses from human infants: pure-tone masking profiles for clicks and filtered clicks.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: clicks and filtered clicks with pure-tone maskers (ABR)
Outcome: infant masking profiles show greater low-frequency contribution than adult profiles
Evidence_Quote: Masking profiles at two intensities (60 and 40 dBn HL) were obtained for click, as well as 4000- and 1000-Hz filtered-click stimuli.

Title: Frequency and intensity discrimination in human infants and adults.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: 1.0-kHz tone bursts with frequency/intensity increments and decrements
Outcome: infant frequency DLs 11-29 Hz and intensity DLs 3-12 dB, larger than adults; no infant discriminated intensity decrements
Evidence_Quote: Subjects were visually reinforced for responding to frequency increments, frequency decrements, intensity increments, or intensity decrements in an ongoing train of 1.0-kHz tone bursts, and stimulus control was monitored using randomly interleaved probe and catch trials.

Title: Exploring the effect of attention on the acoustic change complex: cross-condition reliability and between-subject variability.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: 1 kHz sound stimuli with 10% frequency change (acoustic change complex)
Outcome: no attention effect on ACC latencies or amplitudes; good cross-condition reliability
