Evidence_Quote: ACC responses were recorded via EEG from thirteen normal hearing adults (22-31 years), both with (Attend) and without (Ignore) a counting task designed to direct attention toward 1 kHz sound stimuli containing a 10% frequency change (2000 ms pre-transition duration; 128 trials).

Title: Auditory handicap of hearing impairment and the limited benefit of hearing aids.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: none (theoretical model of hearing impairment)
Outcome: class D hearing loss is about one-third of total hearing loss; hearing aids compensate class A losses only
Evidence_Quote: The latter class represents the first stage of auditory handicap, beginning at an average hearing loss of about 24 dB.

Title: An analysis of auditory brainstem responses in infants.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: filtered clicks (ABR)
Outcome: wave I, III and V latencies decrease with age, largest for wave V and for 1 kHz clicks
Evidence_Quote: Filtered clicks of 1, 2, 4 and 8 kHz were presented at two intensities, 30 and 50 dB HL re the average threshold for a group of young adults.

Title: Gap detection in infants, children, and adults.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: 500-Hz Gaussian-enveloped tone pips (gap detection)
Outcome: gap-detection thresholds 11 ms (infants), 5.6 ms (children), 5.2 ms (adults)
Evidence_Quote: Listeners who were 6.5 months, 12 months, 5 years, and 21 years of age were required to discriminate a pair of 500-Hz, Gaussian-enveloped tone pips from a short 500-Hz tone of the same duration and total energy.

Title: The postnatal development of frequency-place code and tuning characteristics in the auditory midbrain of the phyllostomid bat, Carollia perspicillata.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: acoustic stimulation (inferior colliculus recordings)
Outcome: newborn hearing range 8-76 kHz, about 65% of the adult range; tonotopy develops postnatally
Evidence_Quote: The experimental animal, Carollia perspicillata, has an adult hearing range of 7-110 kHz (characteristic frequencies) but lack any significant overrepresentation of a limited frequency band as known for rhinolophoid bats and Pteronotus.

Title: Recovery of auditory function and structure in the chick after two intense pure tone exposures.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: neonatal chicks (exposed at 2 or 16 days of age)
Stimulus_Type: pure tone exposure (0.9 kHz at 120 dB SPL for 48 h)
Outcome: threshold loss about 57 dB recovering to about 15 dB by 12 days; tectorial membrane regeneration
Evidence_Quote: Groups of neonatal chicks were examined in three experimental conditions that differed in the age and number of times they were exposed to a pure tone of 0.9 kHz at 120 dB SPL for 48 h.

Title: Development of hearing in neonatal rats: air and bone conducted ABR thresholds.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: air- and bone-conducted ABR stimuli
Outcome: air-bone gap disappeared by PND 15; conductive and sensorineural immaturities
Evidence_Quote: ABR to maximal intensity BC stimuli (55 dB above adult rat ABR threshold--55 dB HL*) could be recorded from PND 7-8 while AC responses to 80 dB HL* stimuli, only from PND 11.

Title: Behavioral measures of auditory thresholds in developing tree shrews (Tupaia belangeri).
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: tones (behavioral hearing thresholds)
Outcome: hearing onset at day 16-18 after birth; thresholds adult-like by day 38
Evidence_Quote: The development of hearing in tree shrews (Tupaia belangeri) was tested through behavioral measures in the range of 0.3-60 kHz from the first postnatal thresholds detectable through to those of weanlings.

Title: Critical ages in brainstem development revealed by neonatal 3-channel Lissajous' trajectory of auditory brainstem evoked potentials.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: clicks (auditory brainstem evoked potentials)
Outcome: ABEP thresholds reach adult values by about 35 weeks of gestation
Evidence_Quote: ABEPs were evoked by alternating polarity, monaural 75 dBnHL clicks presented at rates of 10/s, 55/s and 80/s. Potentials were also recorded to 45 dBnHL and 15 dBnHL clicks presented at 10/s.

Title: Estimating the contribution of non-sensory factors to infant-adult differences in behavioral thresholds.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: infants 8 to 11 months old and adults
Stimulus_Type: 1 kHz tone in masking noise
Outcome: infant-adult threshold difference 12 dB, of which 8 dB attributed to sensory and 4 dB to non-sensory factors
Evidence_Quote: In this investigation, thresholds in quiet and in increasing levels of a masking noise for a 1 kHz tone, in infants 8 to 11 months old and in adults, were determined.

Title: Anatomical correlates of the passive properties underlying the developmental shift in the frequency map of the mammalian cochlea.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: none (anatomical measurements of the cochlea)
Outcome: basilar membrane dimensions unchanged as the place code shifts; organ of Corti size and fiber band thickness change
Evidence_Quote: regions that code for the roughly the same frequency (e.g., approximately 11.2 kHz) at different ages can have basilar membranes of very different dimensions.

Title: Auditory threshold sensitivity of the human neonate as measured by the auditory brainstem response.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: healthy full-term human neonates and young adults
Stimulus_Type: clicks and tone-bursts in notched noise (ABR)
Outcome: infant ABR thresholds elevated 3-25 dB relative to adults, greatest at high frequencies
Evidence_Quote: ABRs were elicited with clicks and tone-bursts of 0.5, 1.5, 4.0 and 8.0 kHz, embedded in notched noise, in healthy, full-term human neonates and young adults with known, normal-hearing sensitivity.

Title: Temporary threshold shifts induced by low-pass and high-pass filtered noises in fetal sheep in utero.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: nine late gestational age fetal sheep in utero
Stimulus_Type: low-pass and high-pass filtered noise exposure; tone bursts (ABR)
Outcome: noise exposure increased ABR thresholds and wave IV latencies for 0.5 and 1.0 kHz tone bursts
Evidence_Quote: Auditory brainstem responses (ABRs) were obtained from nine late gestational age fetal sheep in utero before and after a 16-h exposure to low-pass (cut-off frequency 1.0 kHz) and high-pass (cut-off frequency 1.0 kHz) noises (approximately 120 dB sound pressure level, recorded in air). Bone-conduction ABRs were elicited by broadband clicks and 0.5, 1.0 and 2.0 kHz tone bursts.

Title: A developmental study of distortion product otoacoustic emission (2f1-f2) suppression in humans.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: 14 adults, 33 term neonates and 85 premature neonates
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE primary tones (suppression)
Outcome: premature neonates show narrower STCs and shallower suppression growth than adults
Evidence_Quote: Premature neonates showed non-adult-like DPOAE suppression at f2 of 1500 and 6000 Hz
